name: Tornado Warning (Example)
summary: EXAMPLE ONLY. A sample workflow for demonstrating work centers and schedules — not a real severe weather procedure.

checklist.title: Before you start
checklist.intro: Example workflow only. It is here to show branching, parallel tracks and scheduling. It is not a severe weather procedure and must not be used in a real emergency.
items: Torches and the first aid kit

question.help: A watch means conditions are possible. A warning means one has been seen or picked up on radar — move people now.
question.label: Alert

steps.title: Confirm the alert
steps.body: Check the weather feed and note the counties named and the time the alert expires.

steps.title: Warning — move now
steps.body: There is no waiting and no checking the sky first. Everyone goes to shelter.

steps.title: Watch — get ready
steps.body: Brief the wardens, clear the outdoor areas and keep the radio on. Do not move people to shelter yet.

steps.title: Sound the shelter alarm
steps.body: Use the severe weather tone, not the fire tone. They mean opposite things — one sends people in, the other out.

steps.title: Announce the shelter areas
steps.body: Name the shelter areas and the quickest route to each. Repeat it twice.

steps.title: Clear the outdoor areas
steps.body: Radio the yard, the dock and the roof. Everyone comes inside, away from windows.

steps.title: Move visitors and contractors
steps.body: Walk the visitor log. People who do not know the building will not know where the shelter is.

steps.title: Shut the doors and dampers
steps.body: Close exterior doors and loading dock doors. Leave the lights on.

steps.title: Take the shelter roll call
steps.body: Count heads in each shelter area against the roster and the visitor log. Report gaps on the radio.

steps.title: Hold until the all-clear
steps.body: Stay in shelter until the warning expires or is cancelled. A gap in the wind is not the all-clear.

steps.title: Check for damage and injuries
steps.body: Send the wardens out in pairs. Report injuries, gas smells, downed lines and blocked exits straight away.

steps.title: Log it and stand down
steps.body: Record the alert times, who sheltered where, and anything found damaged.
